```diff
+import { afterEach, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
+import type { FlatRow } from '../engine/flatten';
+import { movedBy, pageStepRows } from './key-moves';
+
+// Where a key that moves the active cell takes it (spec phase 6 §3.6), and by how many rows a page key does.
+
+const ROWS = 10;
+const COLUMNS = 4;
+const move = (
+  key: string,
+  place: { row: number; column: number },
+  options: {
+    mod?: boolean;
+    rows?: number;
+    headRows?: number;
+    footer?: boolean;
+    page?: number;
+  } = {},
+) =>
+  movedBy(
+    key,
+    options.mod ?? false,
+    place,
+    options.rows ?? ROWS,
+    COLUMNS,
+    options.headRows ?? 1,
+    () => options.page ?? 3,
+    options.footer ?? false,
+  );
+
+describe('movedBy', () => {
+  it('stops at the edges', () => {
+    expect(move('ArrowLeft', { row: 2, column: 0 })).toEqual({ row: 2, column: 0 });
+    expect(move('ArrowRight', { row: 2, column: 3 })).toEqual({ row: 2, column: 3 });
+    expect(move('ArrowUp', { row: -1, column: 1 })).toEqual({ row: -1, column: 1 });
+    expect(move('ArrowDown', { row: ROWS - 1, column: 1 })).toEqual({ row: ROWS - 1, column: 1 });
+  });
+
+  it('goes up into the filter row, and down from the heading to the first row', () => {
+    expect(move('ArrowUp', { row: 0, column: 1 }, { headRows: 2 })).toEqual({ row: -1, column: 1 });
+    expect(move('ArrowUp', { row: -1, column: 1 }, { headRows: 2 })).toEqual({
+      row: -2,
+      column: 1,
+    });
+    expect(move('ArrowUp', { row: -2, column: 1 }, { headRows: 2 })).toEqual({
+      row: -2,
+      column: 1,
+    });
+    expect(move('ArrowDown', { row: -1, column: 1 })).toEqual({ row: 0, column: 1 });
+  });
+
+  it('takes no arrow or page key with the modifier', () => {
+    for (const key of ['ArrowLeft', 'ArrowRight', 'ArrowUp', 'ArrowDown', 'PageDown', 'PageUp']) {
+      expect(move(key, { row: 2, column: 1 }, { mod: true })).toBeNull();
+    }
+  });
+
+  it('goes to the ends of the row with Home and End, and of the grid with the modifier', () => {
+    expect(move('Home', { row: 4, column: 2 })).toEqual({ row: 4, column: 0 });
+    expect(move('End', { row: 4, column: 2 })).toEqual({ row: 4, column: COLUMNS - 1 });
+    expect(move('Home', { row: 4, column: 2 }, { mod: true })).toEqual({ row: 0, column: 0 });
+    expect(move('End', { row: 4, column: 2 }, { mod: true })).toEqual({
+      row: ROWS - 1,
+      column: COLUMNS - 1,
+    });
+  });
+
+  it('keeps the place with the modifier and no row', () => {
+    const place = { row: -1, column: 2 };
+    expect(move('Home', place, { mod: true, rows: 0 })).toEqual(place);
+    expect(move('End', place, { mod: true, rows: 0 })).toEqual(place);
+  });
+
+  it('stops mod+End at the last row of the body, which the footer is not, and ArrowDown reaches it', () => {
+    // 10 rows and the footer: the list is 11 places long.
+    expect(move('End', { row: 2, column: 0 }, { mod: true, rows: 11, footer: true })).toEqual({
+      row: 9,
+      column: COLUMNS - 1,
+    });
+    expect(move('ArrowDown', { row: 9, column: 0 }, { rows: 11, footer: true })).toEqual({
+      row: 10,
+      column: 0,
+    });
+  });
+
+  it('moves by a page, stops at the last row of the body, and does nothing in the footer', () => {
+    expect(move('PageDown', { row: 2, column: 1 })).toEqual({ row: 5, column: 1 });
+    expect(move('PageDown', { row: 8, column: 1 })).toEqual({ row: 9, column: 1 });
+    expect(move('PageDown', { row: 8, column: 1 }, { rows: 11, footer: true })).toEqual({
+      row: 9,
+      column: 1,
+    });
+    expect(move('PageDown', { row: 10, column: 1 }, { rows: 11, footer: true })).toEqual({
+      row: 10,
+      column: 1,
+    });
+    expect(move('PageDown', { row: -1, column: 1 }, { rows: 0 })).toEqual({ row: -1, column: 1 });
+    expect(move('PageUp', { row: 5, column: 1 })).toEqual({ row: 2, column: 1 });
+    expect(move('PageUp', { row: 1, column: 1 })).toEqual({ row: 0, column: 1 });
+    expect(move('PageUp', { row: -1, column: 1 })).toEqual({ row: -1, column: 1 });
+  });
+
+  it('asks for the page from the row the place is on, in the direction of the key', () => {
+    const asked: [number, number][] = [];
+    const page = (from: number, direction: 1 | -1) => {
+      asked.push([from, direction]);
+      return 2;
+    };
+    movedBy('PageDown', false, { row: 3, column: 0 }, ROWS, COLUMNS, 1, page, false);
+    movedBy('PageUp', false, { row: 6, column: 0 }, ROWS, COLUMNS, 1, page, false);
+    expect(asked).toEqual([
+      [3, 1],
+      [6, -1],
+    ]);
+  });
+
+  it('is no move for any other key', () => {
+    expect(move('a', { row: 1, column: 1 })).toBeNull();
+    expect(move('Enter', { row: 1, column: 1 })).toBeNull();
+  });
+});
+
+describe('pageStepRows', () => {
+  const tables: HTMLTableElement[] = [];
+  afterEach(() => {
+    for (const table of tables.splice(0)) table.remove();
+  });
+
+  // The room for the rows is the frame less the heading: 200px here.
+  const ROOM = 200;
+  const asRows = (kinds: readonly string[]) =>
+    kinds.map((kind, key) => ({ kind, key }) as unknown as FlatRow<unknown>);
+
+  // jsdom has no layout: the heights are given to the elements the step reads them from.
+  function drawn(kinds: readonly ('data' | 'group')[], heights: { data: number; group: number }) {
+    const table = document.createElement('table');
+    const head = table.createTHead();
+    head.insertRow();
+    Object.defineProperty(head, 'offsetHeight', { value: 40 });
+    const body = table.createTBody();
+    for (const kind of kinds) {
+      const row = body.insertRow();
+      row.className = kind === 'data' ? 'flg-data-grid-row' : 'flg-data-grid-group-row';
+      Object.defineProperty(row, 'offsetHeight', { value: heights[kind] });
+    }
+    document.body.append(table);
+    tables.push(table);
+    const frame = document.createElement('div');
+    Object.defineProperty(frame, 'clientHeight', { value: 40 + ROOM });
+    return { table, frame, rows: asRows(kinds) };
+  }
+
+  it('counts the rows that fit between the heading and the bottom of the frame', () => {
+    const { table, frame, rows } = drawn(Array(20).fill('data'), { data: 40, group: 30 });
+    expect(pageStepRows(table, frame, rows, 0, 1)).toBe(5);
+    expect(pageStepRows(table, frame, rows, 10, -1)).toBe(5);
+  });
+
+  it('counts a group row by its own, lower height: a page is more rows where there are groups', () => {
+    const kinds = ['group', 'group', 'group', 'data', 'data', 'data', 'data'] as const;
+    const { table, frame, rows } = drawn(kinds, { data: 40, group: 20 });
+    // Three groups of 20px and three data rows of 40px are 180px, and the fourth data row is over 200px.
+    expect(pageStepRows(table, frame, rows, 0, 1)).toBe(6);
+    const same = drawn(Array(7).fill('data'), { data: 40, group: 20 });
+    expect(pageStepRows(same.table, same.frame, same.rows, 0, 1)).toBe(5);
+  });
+
+  it('is one row with no frame, and with no row drawn', () => {
+    const { table, rows } = drawn(Array(5).fill('data'), { data: 40, group: 30 });
+    expect(pageStepRows(table, null, rows, 0, 1)).toBe(1);
+    const none = drawn([], { data: 40, group: 30 });
+    expect(pageStepRows(none.table, none.frame, none.rows, 0, 1)).toBe(1);
+  });
+
+  it('takes the height of the other kind for a kind that is not drawn', () => {
+    // Only data rows are drawn (a virtual window), and the list holds group rows: they are 40px too.
+    const { table, frame } = drawn(Array(5).fill('data'), { data: 40, group: 30 });
+    const rows = asRows(Array(7).fill('group'));
+    expect(pageStepRows(table, frame, rows, 0, 1)).toBe(5);
+  });
+});
```

```diff
+import type { Dispatch, KeyboardEvent, RefObject, SetStateAction } from 'react';
+import { isLetterKey } from '../../../internal/letter-key';
+import { isMenuKey } from '../../../internal/menu-key';
+import { isApplePlatform } from '../../../internal/platform';
+import { hasModifier } from '../../../internal/roving';
+import { isDataColumn } from '../engine/columns';
+import type { ResolvedColumn } from '../engine/columns';
+import type { FlatRow } from '../engine/flatten';
+import { RESIZE_KEY_STEP } from '../engine/layout';
+import {
+  FILTER_VALUE_SELECTOR,
+  focusInto,
+  homeOf,
+  isFilterPlace,
+  isTitlePlace,
+  rowAt,
+} from '../grid-dom';
+import type { DataGridKey, DataGridSelectionMode } from '../types';
+import type { ActivePlace } from './grid-place';
+import { movedBy, pageStepRows } from './key-moves';
+
+/**
+ * What the keyboard hook hands to the handlers of the keys: the rows and the columns as they are in this
+ * render, the actions a key may take (the hook's own, which read the latest place as the keyboard always
+ * did) and the callbacks the grid was given. The same closures the keys used when `onKeyDown` held them.
+ */
+export interface KeyEnv<TRow> {
+  rows: readonly FlatRow<TRow>[];
+  columns: readonly ResolvedColumn<TRow>[];
+  headRows: number;
+  /** The place past the last row, where the footer of totals is; `null` with no footer place. */
+  footerAt: number | null;
+  /** Whether the grid has no row because of its filter, so its body is the one empty cell. */
+  emptyCell: boolean;
+  /** The scroll frame, read when a page key asks how many rows fit. */
+  frameRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>;
+  /** Makes the place the active one. */
+  choose: (target: ActivePlace) => void;
+  /** Focuses the cell of a place, or asks for its row to be drawn first. */
+  focusPlace: (target: ActivePlace | null) => void;
+  /** Holds a row of the window while the focus moves to a row that is not drawn yet. */
+  setHeld: Dispatch<SetStateAction<number | undefined>>;
+  /** The controls of a cell, which the grid released from the Tab order. */
+  controlsOf: (cell: HTMLElement) => HTMLElement[];
+  reveal: ((index: number) => void) | undefined;
+  onSortPress: (columnId: string, additive: boolean) => void;
+  onResizeBy: (columnId: string, delta: number) => void;
+  onMoveBy: (columnId: string, step: -1 | 1) => void;
+  onMoveRow: ((key: DataGridKey, step: -1 | 1, repeat: boolean) => void) | undefined;
+  onOpenMenu: (columnId: string) => void;
+  onRowActivate: ((row: TRow, key: DataGridKey) => void) | undefined;
+  onToggleGroup: (key: string) => void;
+  selection: {
+    mode: DataGridSelectionMode;
+    press: (key: DataGridKey, range: boolean) => void;
+    chooseAll: () => void;
+  } | null;
+}
+
+/** One key press, with what a handler reads of it: the event, the place and its cell, the modifiers. */
+export interface KeyContext<TRow> extends KeyEnv<TRow> {
+  event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLTableElement>;
+  table: HTMLTableElement;
+  /** The element the event came from, inside `cell`. */
+  target: Element;
+  place: ActivePlace;
+  /** The element of the place: a cell, or the row itself for a group row. */
+  cell: HTMLElement;
+  /** What has the focus when the cell does: the cell, or its box. */
+  home: HTMLElement;
+  /** The row of the place; `undefined` in the heading, the empty cell and a footer that has no row. */
+  row: FlatRow<TRow> | undefined;
+  column: ResolvedColumn<TRow>;
+  /** The key of the platform's modifier, with Shift, Alt and the other modifier up. */
+  mod: boolean;
+  /** The platform's modifier is down, the other one is not (Shift and Alt are not looked at). */
+  modifier: boolean;
+  otherModifier: boolean;
+  /** No modifier, Shift included. */
+  bare: boolean;
+  /** The place is on the titles, and not on the filter row. */
+  onTitle: boolean;
+  /** The place is on the filter row. */
+  onFilter: boolean;
+}
+
+/** The context of the key press at `place`, whose element is `cell` and which came from `target`. */
+export function createKeyContext<TRow>(
+  env: KeyEnv<TRow>,
+  event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLTableElement>,
+  place: ActivePlace,
+  cell: HTMLElement,
+): KeyContext<TRow> {
+  const modifier = isApplePlatform() ? event.metaKey : event.ctrlKey;
+  const otherModifier = isApplePlatform() ? event.ctrlKey : event.metaKey;
+  return {
+    ...env,
+    event,
+    table: event.currentTarget,
+    target: event.target as Element,
+    place,
+    cell,
+    home: homeOf(cell),
+    row: place.row >= 0 ? env.rows[place.row] : undefined,
+    column: env.columns[place.column]!,
+    modifier,
+    otherModifier,
+    mod: modifier && !otherModifier && !event.altKey && !event.shiftKey,
+    bare: !hasModifier(event) && !event.shiftKey,
+    onTitle: isTitlePlace(place.row, env.headRows),
+    onFilter: isFilterPlace(place.row, env.headRows),
+  };
+}
+
+/**
+ * A control of the cell has the focus: the keys are its own, but for Tab, Esc and F2. Takes the event
+ * whenever the focus is not on the cell's home, whether or not it cancelled it.
+ */
+export function widgetKeys<TRow>(keys: KeyContext<TRow>): boolean {
+  const { event, target, cell, home, controlsOf } = keys;
+  if (target === home) return false;
+  if (hasModifier(event)) return true;
+  // A control whose popup is open (a Select) keeps Esc, which the browser answers by closing the
+  // popup and which no handler cancels; the next Esc is the grid's.
+  const popupOpen = target.closest('[aria-expanded="true"]');
+  if (event.key === 'Escape' ? !(popupOpen && cell.contains(popupOpen)) : event.key === 'F2') {
+    event.preventDefault();
+    focusInto(home, cell);
+  } else if (event.key === 'Tab') {
+    const controls = controlsOf(cell);
+    const at = controls.findIndex((control) => control === target || control.contains(target));
+    if (controls.length === 0 || at < 0) return true;
+    event.preventDefault();
+    const next = controls[(at + (event.shiftKey ? controls.length - 1 : 1)) % controls.length]!;
+    focusInto(next, cell);
+  }
+  return true;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The keys of the heading: Enter on a title sorts, and Shift+Enter keeps the other columns' sort and adds
+ * this one; Space is cancelled; the keys of the columns on the title of a data column (resize, move, the
+ * menu). The titles have the keys of the columns; the filter row, which is no title, has none of them.
+ */
+export function headingKeys<TRow>(keys: KeyContext<TRow>): boolean {
+  const { event, place, cell, home, column, onTitle, modifier, otherModifier } = keys;
+  const handled = (): void => event.preventDefault();
+  // The box in the title of the column of boxes is its home and its one control: Enter presses it, as
+  // it presses the box of a row, and Shift+Enter does nothing there.
+  if (event.key === 'Enter' && onTitle && !hasModifier(event)) {
+    if (home !== cell) {
+      if (event.shiftKey) return true;
+      handled();
+      home.click();
+      return true;
+    }
+    if (!column.allowSorting) return true;
+    handled();
+    keys.onSortPress(column.id, event.shiftKey);
+    return true;
+  }
+  // Space has no job on a cell of the heading (Enter sorts a title, and a filter cell has no key of its
+  // own): it is cancelled, or the browser scrolls the frame or the page a screen down with it. The title
+  // of the column of boxes is not one: its box is the home and the target, and keeps Space, which
+  // presses it.
+  if (event.key === ' ' && place.row < 0 && home === cell && !hasModifier(event)) {
+    handled();
+    return true;
+  }
+  // The keys of the columns, on the title of a data column (the column of boxes has none). Each one
+  // is cancelled where it does nothing too, a column that cannot be resized for one, so the browser
+  // does nothing with it either (Alt+Shift+arrow selects text in some of them).
+  if (
+    onTitle &&
+    isDataColumn(column) &&
+    event.altKey &&
+    event.shiftKey &&
+    !event.ctrlKey &&
+    !event.metaKey &&
+    (event.key === 'ArrowLeft' || event.key === 'ArrowRight')
+  ) {
+    handled();
+    keys.onResizeBy(column.id, event.key === 'ArrowLeft' ? -RESIZE_KEY_STEP : RESIZE_KEY_STEP);
+    return true;
+  }
+  if (
+    onTitle &&
+    isDataColumn(column) &&
+    modifier &&
+    !otherModifier &&
+    !event.altKey &&
+    event.shiftKey &&
+    (event.key === 'ArrowLeft' || event.key === 'ArrowRight')
+  ) {
+    handled();
+    keys.onMoveBy(column.id, event.key === 'ArrowLeft' ? -1 : 1);
+    return true;
+  }
+  // The menu of the column: `Alt+↓`, `Shift+F10` and the ContextMenu key. Cancelled where the column has
+  // no menu too, and a held key opens it once.
+  if (
+    onTitle &&
+    isDataColumn(column) &&
+    (isMenuKey(event) ||
+      (event.key === 'ArrowDown' &&
+        event.altKey &&
+        !event.shiftKey &&
+        !event.ctrlKey &&
+        !event.metaKey))
+  ) {
+    handled();
+    if (!event.repeat) keys.onOpenMenu(column.id);
+    return true;
+  }
+  return false;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The keys of the rows: Space on the cell of a row chooses it (Shift: the range to it), and mod+A every row
+ * of the scope, from any cell of the grid, the titles too. A box that has the focus is the cell's
+ * own target, so these are its keys too; the title's box is a control of its own and keeps Space. In a grid
+ * with no row, mod+A on a title is cancelled and does nothing else: there is nothing to choose, and
+ * nothing to say. `mod+Shift+↑` and `mod+Shift+↓` on any cell of a data row move it one place.
+ */
+export function rowKeys<TRow>(keys: KeyContext<TRow>): boolean {
+  const { event, place, cell, home, row, rows, selection, footerAt, modifier, otherModifier } =
+    keys;
+  const handled = (): void => event.preventDefault();
+  if (selection?.mode === 'multiple' && keys.mod && isLetterKey(event, 'a')) {
+    handled();
+    if (rows.length > 0) selection.chooseAll();
+    return true;
+  }
+  // Space has no job on a group row, a detail row or the footer, and is cancelled, or the browser scrolls a
+  // screen down with it. On the button of a detail, and on the handle of a row, it is the button's: it
+  // opens or closes the detail, or opens the row menu, and chooses no row.
+  const service = home !== cell ? cell.getAttribute('data-service') : null;
+  const onToggle = service === 'detail' || service === 'drag';
+  if (
+    (row?.kind === 'group' || row?.kind === 'detail' || place.row === footerAt) &&
+    event.key === ' ' &&
+    !hasModifier(event)
+  ) {
+    handled();
+    return true;
+  }
+  if (selection && row?.kind === 'data' && !onToggle && event.key === ' ' && !hasModifier(event)) {
+    handled();
+    selection.press(row.key, event.shiftKey && selection.mode === 'multiple');
+    return true;
+  }
+  // The keys of a row: each is cancelled where the row cannot go that way too, so the browser does
+  // nothing with it either.
+  if (
+    keys.onMoveRow &&
+    row?.kind === 'data' &&
+    modifier &&
+    !otherModifier &&
+    !event.altKey &&
+    event.shiftKey &&
+    (event.key === 'ArrowUp' || event.key === 'ArrowDown')
+  ) {
+    handled();
+    keys.onMoveRow(row.key, event.key === 'ArrowUp' ? -1 : 1, event.repeat);
+    return true;
+  }
+  return false;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The keys of a group row (the tree grid pattern of the APG): Enter toggles it, → opens a closed one
+ * or goes to its first row, ← closes an open one or goes to the group above, Home and End go to the
+ * first and the last row of the list. The column the place remembers never changes on a group row.
+ */
+export function groupRowKeys<TRow>(keys: KeyContext<TRow>): boolean {
+  const { event, place, row, rows, table, reveal, bare, choose, focusPlace } = keys;
+  if (row?.kind !== 'group' || !bare) return false;
+  const handled = (): void => event.preventDefault();
+  const to = (at: number): void => {
+    const target = { row: at, column: place.column };
+    if (reveal && !rowAt(table, at)) keys.setHeld(place.row);
+    choose(target);
+    focusPlace(target);
+  };
+  if (event.key === 'Enter') {
+    handled();
+    // A held key repeats: one press is one toggle.
+    if (!event.repeat) keys.onToggleGroup(row.key);
+    return true;
+  }
+  if (event.key === 'ArrowRight') {
+    handled();
+    if (!row.expanded) keys.onToggleGroup(row.key);
+    else if (rows[place.row + 1]) to(place.row + 1);
+    return true;
+  }
+  if (event.key === 'ArrowLeft') {
+    handled();
+    if (row.expanded) {
+      keys.onToggleGroup(row.key);
+      return true;
+    }
+    for (let at = place.row - 1; at >= 0; at--) {
+      const above = rows[at]!;
+      if (above.kind === 'group' && above.level < row.level) {
+        to(at);
+        return true;
+      }
+    }
+    return true;
+  }
+  if (event.key === 'Home' || event.key === 'End') {
+    handled();
+    const at = event.key === 'Home' ? 0 : rows.length - 1;
+    if (at !== place.row) to(at);
+    return true;
+  }
+  return false;
+}
+
+/**
+ * A detail row is one cell: the keys that move along a row have nowhere to go, and are cancelled, or the
+ * browser scrolls the frame sideways with them. Enter and F2 go into its content; ↑ and ↓ leave it.
+ */
+export function detailRowKeys<TRow>(keys: KeyContext<TRow>): boolean {
+  const { event, row, bare } = keys;
+  if (
+    row?.kind === 'detail' &&
+    bare &&
+    (event.key === 'ArrowLeft' ||
+      event.key === 'ArrowRight' ||
+      event.key === 'Home' ||
+      event.key === 'End')
+  ) {
+    event.preventDefault();
+    return true;
+  }
+  return false;
+}
+
+/** Enter and F2: into the controls of the cell, the press of its box, or the activation of the row. */
+export function enterKeys<TRow>(keys: KeyContext<TRow>): boolean {
+  const { event, place, cell, home, row, onFilter, footerAt, controlsOf } = keys;
+  if (event.key !== 'Enter' && event.key !== 'F2') return false;
+  if (!keys.bare) return true;
+  // The footer holds nothing to go into or to activate.
+  if (place.row === footerAt) return true;
+  // The box of a cell is its one control, and Enter presses it as it would a button.
+  if (home !== cell && event.key === 'Enter') {
+    event.preventDefault();
+    home.click();
+    return true;
+  }
+  const controls = controlsOf(cell);
+  // A filter cell goes into its value, the input or the Select, and not into the operator button that
+  // comes before the input: the operator is one Tab away.
+  const first = onFilter
+    ? (controls.find((control) => control.matches(FILTER_VALUE_SELECTOR)) ?? controls[0])
+    : controls[0];
+  if (first) {
+    event.preventDefault();
+    focusInto(first, cell);
+  } else if (event.key === 'Enter' && place.row >= 0 && keys.onRowActivate) {
+    // A group row is handled above, and a detail row is no row of data to activate: Enter does nothing there.
+    if (row?.kind !== 'data') return true;
+    event.preventDefault();
+    keys.onRowActivate(row.row, row.key);
+  }
+  return true;
+}
+
+/** The keys that move the active cell: arrows, Home, End and the page keys. */
+export function moveKeys<TRow>(keys: KeyContext<TRow>): boolean {
+  const { event, place, rows, columns, table, footerAt, mod, choose, focusPlace } = keys;
+  // The empty cell is one cell across every column: ↑ goes back to the title of the column the place
+  // was at, and the keys that move along a row have nowhere to go.
+  const onEmpty = rows.length === 0 && place.row === 0;
+  const moved = movedBy(
+    event.key,
+    mod,
+    place,
+    rows.length === 0 && keys.emptyCell ? 1 : rows.length + (footerAt !== null ? 1 : 0),
+    columns.length,
+    keys.headRows,
+    (from, direction) => pageStepRows(table, keys.frameRef.current, rows, from, direction),
+    footerAt !== null,
+  );
+  const next = moved && onEmpty ? { ...moved, column: place.column } : moved;
+  if (!next) return false;
+  event.preventDefault();
+  if (next.row !== place.row || next.column !== place.column) {
+    // The row the focus is on stays drawn until it has moved, which for a row that is not drawn yet
+    // is after the commit that draws it.
+    const inBody = (row: number) => row >= 0 && row < rows.length;
+    if (keys.reveal && inBody(place.row) && inBody(next.row) && !rowAt(table, next.row)) {
+      keys.setHeld(place.row);
+    }
+    choose(next);
+    focusPlace(next);
+  }
+  return true;
+}
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/hooks/grid-place.ts b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/grid-place.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..45ae053
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/grid-place.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,143 @@
+import { clamp } from '../../../internal/number';
+import type { FlatRow } from '../engine/flatten';
+import { groupKey } from '../engine/group';
+import { sameList } from '../engine/selection';
+import type { DataGridKey } from '../types';
+
+/**
+ * Where the keyboard is in the grid: a column title, a cell of the filter row, a cell of a data row or a
+ * group row, or the empty cell of a grid whose filter keeps no row, said by what they are and not by where
+ * they are drawn (a row's kind and key, and a column id), so a sort, a page, a window or a filter row that
+ * comes or goes does not lose the place. A body place holds the keys of the groups its row is inside (for a
+ * group row, the groups above it): when its row goes because one of them closed, the place goes to the
+ * nearest of them that is still in the list.
+ */
+export type ActiveCell =
+  | { area: 'header'; column: string }
+  | { area: 'filter'; column: string }
+  | {
+      area: 'body';
+      key: DataGridKey;
+      kind: FlatRow<unknown>['kind'];
+      groups: readonly string[];
+      column: string;
+    }
+  | { area: 'empty'; column: string }
+  | { area: 'footer'; column: string };
+
+/**
+ * The keys of the groups the row at `index` is inside, the outermost first; for a group row, the groups
+ * above it, and for a detail row, those of its master, the row before it.
+ */
+export function groupsAbove(rows: readonly FlatRow<unknown>[], index: number): readonly string[] {
+  const row = rows[index]!;
+  if (row.kind === 'data') return row.groups;
+  if (row.kind === 'detail') {
+    const master = rows[index - 1];
+    return master?.kind === 'data' ? master.groups : [];
+  }
+  const { path } = row.node;
+  return Array.from({ length: path.length - 1 }, (_, at) => groupKey(path.slice(0, at + 1)));
+}
+
+/** A row of the list is the row of a place when its kind and its key are: a group key is no data key. */
+export const isRowOf = (
+  row: FlatRow<unknown> | undefined,
+  cell: { key: DataGridKey; kind: string },
+) => row !== undefined && row.kind === cell.kind && row.key === cell.key;
+
+/**
+ * The active cell as places in the drawn grid: `row` counts the heading rows up from the body (-1 the last
+ * heading row, the filter row when there is one, else the titles; -2 the titles when there is a filter row:
+ * `isTitlePlace` and `isFilterPlace` say which), else it is an index of `rows`; a grid with no row whose
+ * filter is the reason has the one place 0 in its body, its empty cell. The row of the footer is the place
+ * just past the last row of the list: `rows.length`.
+ */
+export interface ActivePlace {
+  row: number;
+  column: number;
+}
+
+export interface Position {
+  /** What was chosen, or `null` before anything was: the first cell of the first row. */
+  cell: ActiveCell | null;
+  /** The index its row had when last seen, which is where the place goes when the row leaves. */
+  index: number;
+  /** The index its column had when last seen, which is where the place goes when the column leaves. */
+  columnIndex: number;
+}
+
+export function samePlace(a: ActivePlace | null, b: ActivePlace | null): boolean {
+  return a === b || (a !== null && b !== null && a.row === b.row && a.column === b.column);
+}
+
+/** Two positions are one when they say the same place, the groups of a body place included. */
+export function samePosition(a: Position, b: Position): boolean {
+  if (
+    a.index !== b.index ||
+    a.columnIndex !== b.columnIndex ||
+    a.cell?.area !== b.cell?.area ||
+    a.cell?.column !== b.cell?.column
+  ) {
+    return false;
+  }
+  return (
+    a.cell?.area !== 'body' ||
+    (b.cell?.area === 'body' &&
+      a.cell.key === b.cell.key &&
+      a.cell.kind === b.cell.kind &&
+      sameList(a.cell.groups, b.cell.groups))
+  );
+}
+
+/**
+ * The place the position has now. A row that is gone leaves the place at the same index, as far as
+ * the rows reach, and at the title of its column when none is left, or at the empty cell when the
+ * grid is empty because of its filter (`emptyCell`: the button that clears it is the one place of
+ * the body); a column that is gone leaves it at the column now at the index it had, as far as the
+ * columns reach (spec phase 6 §3.6). A place in the titles stays in them when a filter row comes or
+ * goes, and one in the filter row, when it goes, is the title of its column (`headRows` is how many
+ * heading rows there are). Nothing chosen yet is the first cell of the first row, or the empty
+ * cell, or the first title; a position at the empty cell, once rows are back, is the first cell of
+ * the first row. The row at the index last seen is the one when it has the key: of two rows with
+ * the same key (the grid warns), the second is then not taken for the first, which would leave its
+ * keys to nobody. A detail row that is gone (its detail closed, or its master left) leaves the place on its
+ * master row, at the column the place remembers, when the master is still in the list. A row that is gone
+ * because a group closed leaves the place at the nearest of its groups that is still in the list, which is
+ * that group's row. A place in the footer (`footer`: the grid
+ * has one and a row to stand over) is the place past the last row; with no footer, or no row, it is the
+ * last row, or the title when there is none.
+ */
+export function resolvePlace(
+  position: Position,
+  rows: readonly FlatRow<unknown>[],
+  columns: readonly { id: string }[],
+  emptyCell = false,
+  headRows = 1,
+  footer = false,
+): ActivePlace | null {
+  if (columns.length === 0) return null;
+  const { cell } = position;
+  const at = columns.findIndex((candidate) => candidate.id === cell?.column);
+  const column = at >= 0 ? at : clamp(position.columnIndex, 0, columns.length - 1);
+  if (cell?.area === 'header') return { row: -headRows, column };
+  // The filter row is the last heading row; without one that row is the titles, where the place stays.
+  if (cell?.area === 'filter') return { row: -1, column };
+  if (rows.length === 0) return { row: emptyCell ? 0 : -headRows, column };
+  if (cell === null) return { row: 0, column };
+  if (cell.area === 'footer') return { row: footer ? rows.length : rows.length - 1, column };
+  // The empty cell has no column of its own: the rows that come back start at their first cell.
+  if (cell.area === 'empty') return { row: 0, column: 0 };
+  if (isRowOf(rows[position.index], cell)) return { row: position.index, column };
+  const found = rows.findIndex((row) => isRowOf(row, cell));
+  if (found >= 0) return { row: found, column };
+  if (cell.kind === 'detail') {
+    const master = rows.findIndex((row) => row.kind === 'data' && row.key === cell.key);
+    if (master >= 0) return { row: master, column };
+  }
+  for (let at = cell.groups.length - 1; at >= 0; at--) {
+    const group = rows.findIndex((row) => row.kind === 'group' && row.key === cell.groups[at]);
+    if (group >= 0) return { row: group, column };
+  }
+  return { row: Math.min(position.index, rows.length - 1), column };
+}
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/hooks/grid-pointer.ts b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/grid-pointer.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..fc32169
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/grid-pointer.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,144 @@
+import type { MouseEvent } from 'react';
+import { takesOwnPress } from '../../../internal/controls';
+import type { FlatRow } from '../engine/flatten';
+import {
+  addsLevel,
+  cellsOf,
+  EMPTY_PLACE_SELECTOR,
+  focusHomeOf,
+  GRID_SELECTOR,
+  homeOf,
+  isOwn,
+  listIndexOf,
+  listRows,
+  ownCell,
+  titleRow,
+} from '../grid-dom';
+import type { DataGridKey } from '../types';
+import type { ActivePlace } from './grid-place';
+
+/** What the presses of the pointer read of the keyboard hook: the rows, the footer and where to put the place. */
+export interface PointerContext<TRow> {
+  rows: readonly FlatRow<TRow>[];
+  /** The place past the last row, where the footer of totals is; `null` with no footer place. */
+  footerAt: number | null;
+  /** Makes the place the active one. */
+  choose: (target: ActivePlace) => void;
+  /** The column the active place remembers, read when a press needs it: 0 before there is one. */
+  column: () => number;
+  onRowActivate: ((row: TRow, key: DataGridKey) => void) | undefined;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Makes the cell `target` is in (a press on it, or the focus that came to it) the active place. A group
+ * row, a detail row, the empty cell and the footer are each one place, whichever part is pressed.
+ */
+export function activate<TRow>(
+  pointer: PointerContext<TRow>,
+  target: Element,
+  table: HTMLTableElement,
+): void {
+  const { choose, column, footerAt } = pointer;
+  // A group row is one place, whichever part of it is pressed or has the focus: the column stays.
+  const groupRow = target.closest('tr.flg-data-grid-group-row');
+  if (groupRow && groupRow.closest(GRID_SELECTOR) === table) {
+    const tr = groupRow as HTMLTableRowElement;
+    choose({
+      row: listIndexOf(tr, listRows(table).indexOf(tr)),
+      column: column(),
+    });
+    return;
+  }
+  const cell = ownCell(target, table);
+  // A detail row is one place, whichever part of it is pressed or has the focus: the column stays.
+  if (cell?.matches('.flg-data-grid-detail-cell')) {
+    const tr = cell.parentElement as HTMLTableRowElement;
+    choose({
+      row: listIndexOf(tr, listRows(table).indexOf(tr)),
+      column: column(),
+    });
+    return;
+  }
+  // The empty cell of a filtered grid is the one place of the body, whichever part of it is pressed.
+  if (cell?.matches(EMPTY_PLACE_SELECTOR)) {
+    choose({ row: 0, column: column() });
+    return;
+  }
+  if (cell?.matches('.flg-data-grid-foot-cell')) {
+    if (footerAt !== null) {
+      choose({
+        row: footerAt,
+        column: cellsOf(cell.parentElement as HTMLTableRowElement).indexOf(cell),
+      });
+    }
+    return;
+  }
+  if (!cell?.matches('.flg-data-grid-head, .flg-data-grid-filter-cell, .flg-data-grid-cell'))
+    return;
+  const tr = cell.parentElement as HTMLTableRowElement;
+  const heading = table.tHead ? Array.from(table.tHead.rows).indexOf(tr) : -1;
+  const inHead = heading >= 0;
+  const drawn = inHead ? -1 : listRows(table).indexOf(tr);
+  if (drawn < 0 && !inHead) return;
+  // A heading row's place counts up from the body: the last row of the heading is -1.
+  const index = inHead ? heading - table.tHead!.rows.length : listIndexOf(tr, drawn);
+  choose({ row: index, column: cellsOf(tr).indexOf(cell) });
+}
+
+/**
+ * A browser that does not focus a button it is pressed on (Safari) says nothing to `onFocus`,
+ * so the press makes its cell active here. Where the browser would put the focus is then held
+ * to the rule of a press (spec phase 6 §3.6): after it the focus is on the home of the active
+ * cell. A control of a cell keeps its own press, and one that a part already took (the sort
+ * button, a row's Shift press) is left as that part left it. A press on the cell of a box, beside
+ * the box, would focus the cell, which is not its home; a press with Shift or the modifier on a
+ * title would start a text selection: both are cancelled and give the focus to the home. A press
+ * on the filler column or on an indent does nothing, and the focus stays: the frame's `tabindex`
+ * would take it.
+ */
+export function pressCell<TRow>(
+  pointer: PointerContext<TRow>,
+  event: MouseEvent<HTMLTableElement>,
+): void {
+  const table = event.currentTarget;
+  if (!isOwn(event.target, table)) return;
+  const target = event.target as Element;
+  activate(pointer, target, table);
+  if (event.button !== 0 || event.defaultPrevented) return;
+  const cell = ownCell(target, table);
+  if (!cell || takesOwnPress({ target, currentTarget: cell })) return;
+  // The filler and the indents are no place: a press on one does nothing, as the active place stays,
+  // and cancelling it keeps the browser from giving the focus to the frame's `tabindex="-1"`. The
+  // indents of a group row are the exception: the row is a place of its own (`tabindex`), and the
+  // press gives it the focus.
+  if (
+    cell.classList.contains('flg-data-grid-filler') ||
+    (cell.classList.contains('flg-data-grid-indent') && !cell.closest('.flg-data-grid-group-row'))
+  ) {
+    event.preventDefault();
+    return;
+  }
+  const onTitles = cell.parentElement === titleRow(table);
+  if (homeOf(cell) !== cell || (onTitles && addsLevel(event))) {
+    event.preventDefault();
+    focusHomeOf(cell);
+  }
+}
+
+/** The double press on the cell of a data row: activates the row, unless a control of the cell took the press. */
+export function pressTwice<TRow>(
+  pointer: PointerContext<TRow>,
+  event: MouseEvent<HTMLTableElement>,
+): void {
+  const { rows, onRowActivate } = pointer;
+  const table = event.currentTarget;
+  if (!onRowActivate || !isOwn(event.target, table)) return;
+  const cell = ownCell(event.target as Element, table);
+  if (!cell?.matches('.flg-data-grid-cell')) return;
+  // The cell is what is pressed: a control in it takes the press, but the cell itself, which is
+  // the Tab stop (`tabindex="0"`) when active, is no control of its row.
+  if (takesOwnPress({ target: event.target, currentTarget: cell })) return;
+  const drawnRow = cell.parentElement as HTMLTableRowElement;
+  const row = rows[listIndexOf(drawnRow, listRows(table).indexOf(drawnRow))];
+  if (row?.kind === 'data') onRowActivate(row.row, row.key);
+}
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/hooks/key-moves.ts b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/key-moves.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..5f8fb73
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/key-moves.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,93 @@
+import { rowsThatFit } from '../engine/virtual';
+import type { FlatRow } from '../engine/flatten';
+import { listRows, rowAt, rowKind } from '../grid-dom';
+import type { ActivePlace } from './grid-place';
+
+/**
+ * How many rows a page key moves by from the row at `from`: the rows that fit between the heading and the
+ * footer (or the bottom of the frame), counted over their own heights (`rowsThatFit`: a group row is lower than a
+ * data row), and at least one. The height of a data row and of a group row is read from a row of the kind
+ * that is drawn; a kind that is not drawn (a virtual grid may draw no group row) has the height of the
+ * other. A detail row is read from its own row: a grid with details draws every row, and its height is the
+ * content's.
+ */
+export function pageStepRows<TRow>(
+  table: HTMLTableElement,
+  frame: HTMLElement | null,
+  rows: readonly FlatRow<TRow>[],
+  from: number,
+  direction: 1 | -1,
+): number {
+  const drawn = listRows(table);
+  const dataHeight = drawn.find((row) => rowKind(row) === 'data')?.offsetHeight ?? 0;
+  const groupHeight = drawn.find((row) => rowKind(row) === 'group')?.offsetHeight ?? 0;
+  const data = dataHeight || groupHeight;
+  const group = groupHeight || dataHeight;
+  if (!frame || data === 0) return 1;
+  const room =
+    frame.clientHeight - (table.tHead?.offsetHeight ?? 0) - (table.tFoot?.offsetHeight ?? 0);
+  return rowsThatFit(
+    (index) => {
+      const kind = rows[index]?.kind;
+      if (kind === 'group') return group;
+      // A grid with details draws every row, so an open detail is read from its own row.
+      if (kind === 'detail') return rowAt(table, index)?.offsetHeight || data;
+      return data;
+    },
+    rows.length,
+    from,
+    direction,
+    room,
+  );
+}
+
+/** Where a key that moves the active cell takes it, or `null` for a key that does not. */
+export function movedBy(
+  key: string,
+  mod: boolean,
+  place: ActivePlace,
+  rowCount: number,
+  columnCount: number,
+  headRows: number,
+  page: (from: number, direction: 1 | -1) => number,
+  footer: boolean,
+): ActivePlace | null {
+  const lastColumn = columnCount - 1;
+  // `rowCount` counts the footer's row too; the keys that go to an end or by a page stop at the last row
+  // of the body, and the footer is reached by `ArrowDown` and left by `ArrowUp` alone.
+  const lastRow = footer ? rowCount - 2 : rowCount - 1;
+  switch (key) {
+    case 'ArrowLeft':
+      return mod ? null : { ...place, column: Math.max(0, place.column - 1) };
+    case 'ArrowRight':
+      return mod ? null : { ...place, column: Math.min(lastColumn, place.column + 1) };
+    case 'ArrowUp':
+      return mod ? null : { ...place, row: Math.max(-headRows, place.row - 1) };
+    case 'ArrowDown':
+      if (mod) return null;
+      // Down the heading rows to the first row; past the last row there is nowhere.
+      return { ...place, row: Math.min(rowCount - 1, place.row + 1) };
+    case 'Home':

+    case 'PageDown':
+      if (mod) return null;

+      // at the last row of the body and does nothing in the footer.
+      return lastRow < 0 || place.row > lastRow

+        : { ...place, row: Math.min(lastRow, place.row + page(place.row, 1)) };
+    case 'PageUp':
+      if (mod) return null;
+      return place.row < 0
+        ? place
+        : { ...place, row: Math.max(0, place.row - page(place.row, -1)) };

+      return null;

diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-grid-context-value.ts b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-grid-context-value.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..b2326dd
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-grid-context-value.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,178 @@
+import { useMemo } from 'react';
+import type { ResolvedColumn } from '../engine/columns';
+import type { TextReader } from '../engine/filter';
+import type { DetailsView, GridContextValue } from '../grid-context';
+import type { PinPlace } from '../engine/layout';
+import type { TableVariant } from '../../table/Table';
+import type {
+  DataGridKey,
+  DataGridLabels,
+  DataGridProps,
+  DataGridSelectAllMode,
+  DataGridSelectionMode,
+} from '../types';
+import type { ColumnDrag } from './use-column-drag';
+import type { ColumnMenuControl } from './use-column-menu';
+import type { ColumnResize } from './use-column-resize';
+import type { SelectionActions } from './use-selection';
+
+export interface GridContextOptions<TRow> {
+  columns: readonly ResolvedColumn<TRow>[];
+  layoutColumns: readonly ResolvedColumn<TRow>[];
+  resolved: readonly ResolvedColumn<TRow>[];
+  /** Opens or closes the group with this key. */
+  toggleGroup: (key: string) => void;
+  /** Whether a row has a detail, `undefined` while the grid has no details. */
+  hasDetail: DetailsView<TRow>['has'] | undefined;
+  renderDetail: DataGridProps<TRow>['renderDetail'];
+  toggleDetail: (key: DataGridKey) => void;
+  groupTotals: GridContextValue<TRow>['groupTotals'];
+  summaryReader: TextReader<TRow>;
+  filler: boolean;
+  fillerAt: number;
+  pins: readonly (PinPlace | undefined)[];
+  layoutPins: readonly (PinPlace | undefined)[];
+  labels: DataGridLabels;
+  variant: TableVariant;
+  locale: string;
+  virtual: boolean;
+  filterRow: boolean;
+  headerFilter: boolean;
+  skeletonRows: number;
+  textOf: (row: TRow, column: ResolvedColumn<TRow>) => string;
+  rowClassName: DataGridProps<TRow>['rowClassName'];
+  sorting: GridContextValue<TRow>['sorting'];
+  onSortPress: (columnId: string, additive: boolean) => void;
+  selectionMode: DataGridSelectionMode;
+  selectAllMode: DataGridSelectAllMode;
+  rowClick: boolean;
+  activates: boolean;
+  selectionActions: SelectionActions;
+  grouped: readonly string[];
+  panel: boolean;
+  rowHeader: ResolvedColumn<TRow> | undefined;
+  /** The `rowReorder` member (`useRowReordering`). */
+  rowReorder: GridContextValue<TRow>['rowReorder'];
+  resize: ColumnResize;
+  reorder: ColumnDrag;
+  columnMenu: ColumnMenuControl;
+  menuId: string;
+  hideable: boolean;
+  groupable: boolean;
+}
+
+/**
+ * What the parts of one grid share (`GridContext`): every member and every dependency a part of the grid
+ * reads, made again only when one of them changes. It holds no row and no chosen key, so a choice, a drag
+ * or a menu opening draws no row.
+ */
+export function useGridContextValue<TRow>(
+  options: GridContextOptions<TRow>,
+): GridContextValue<TRow> {
+  const { columns, layoutColumns, resolved, toggleGroup, hasDetail, renderDetail, toggleDetail } =
+    options;
+  const { groupTotals, summaryReader, filler, fillerAt, pins, layoutPins, labels, variant } =
+    options;
+  const { locale, virtual, filterRow, headerFilter, skeletonRows, textOf, rowClassName } = options;
+  const { sorting, onSortPress, selectionMode, selectAllMode, rowClick, activates } = options;
+  const { selectionActions, grouped, panel, rowHeader, rowReorder, resize, reorder } = options;
+  const { columnMenu, menuId, hideable, groupable } = options;
+  const groupsView = useMemo(() => ({ toggle: toggleGroup }), [toggleGroup]);
+  const detailsView = useMemo<DetailsView<TRow> | null>(
+    () =>
+      hasDetail && typeof renderDetail === 'function'
+        ? { has: hasDetail, render: renderDetail, toggle: toggleDetail }
+        : null,
+    [hasDetail, renderDetail, toggleDetail],
+  );
+  return useMemo<GridContextValue<TRow>>(
+    () => ({
+      columns,
+      layoutColumns,
+      resolved,
+      groups: groupsView,
+      groupTotals,
+      summaryReader,
+      details: detailsView,
+      filler,
+      fillerAt,
+      pins,
+      layoutPins,
+      labels,
+      variant,
+      locale,
+      virtual,
+      filterRow,
+      headerFilter,
+      skeletonRows,
+      textOf,
+      rowClassName,
+      sorting,
+      onSortPress,
+      selection: {
+        mode: selectionMode,
+        allMode: selectAllMode,
+        onRowClick: rowClick,
+        activates,
+        actions: selectionActions,
+      },
+      grouped,
+      groupPanel: panel,
+      rowHeader,
+      rowReorder,
+      resize,
+      reorder: { onPointerDown: reorder.onPointerDown },
+      menu: {
+        store: columnMenu.store,
+        open: columnMenu.open,
+        close: columnMenu.close,
+        onPointerDown: columnMenu.onPointerDown,
+        onContextMenu: columnMenu.onContextMenu,
+        contentId: menuId,
+        hideable,
+        groupable,
+      },
+      dragSource: reorder.source,
+    }),
+    [
+      columns,
+      layoutColumns,
+      resolved,
+      groupsView,
+      groupTotals,
+      summaryReader,
+      detailsView,
+      filler,
+      fillerAt,
+      pins,
+      layoutPins,
+      textOf,
+      rowReorder,
+      labels,
+      locale,
+      variant,
+      virtual,
+      filterRow,
+      headerFilter,
+      skeletonRows,
+      rowClassName,
+      sorting,
+      onSortPress,
+      selectionMode,
+      selectAllMode,
+      rowClick,
+      activates,
+      selectionActions,
+      grouped,
+      panel,
+      rowHeader,
+      resize,
+      reorder.onPointerDown,
+      columnMenu,
+      menuId,
+      hideable,
+      groupable,
+      reorder.source,
+    ],
+  );
+}

diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-grid-summary.ts b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-grid-summary.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..a19daf5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-grid-summary.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,68 @@
+import { useMemo } from 'react';
+import { resolveSummaryItems, sameSummary } from '../engine/summary';
+import type { ResolvedSummaryItem } from '../engine/summary';
+import type { ResolvedColumn } from '../engine/columns';
+import type { DataGridSummaryProp } from '../types';
+import { useSummaryWarning } from './use-renewal-warning';
+import { useKept } from './use-kept';
+
+/** The totals asked for, resolved against the columns, and the part of them the pipeline reads. */
+export interface GridSummary<TRow> {
+  summaryResolved: {
+    total: ResolvedSummaryItem<TRow>[];
+    group: ResolvedSummaryItem<TRow>[];
+    byColumn: Map<string, ResolvedSummaryItem<TRow>[]>;
+    noColumn: boolean;
+    noType: boolean;
+    repeated: boolean;
+  };
+  pipelineSummary: {
+    total: ResolvedSummaryItem<TRow>[];
+    group: ResolvedSummaryItem<TRow>[];
+  } | null;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The totals asked for, kept while the prop says the same (an object written in the JSX is new on every
+ * render, and functions count by identity), and resolved against the columns: each list drops the item
+ * that names no column and the later of two with one id, and says so once, from an effect.
+ */
+export function useGridSummary<TRow>({
+  summary,
+  resolved,
+}: {
+  summary: DataGridSummaryProp<TRow> | undefined;
+  resolved: readonly ResolvedColumn<TRow>[];
+}): GridSummary<TRow> {
+  const summaryKept = useKept(summary, sameSummary);
+  useSummaryWarning(summary);
+  const summaryResolved = useMemo(() => {
+    const total = resolveSummaryItems(summaryKept?.total ?? [], resolved);
+    const group = resolveSummaryItems(summaryKept?.group ?? [], resolved);
+    // The group totals by the column they stand under, for the group rows to find theirs.
+    const byColumn = new Map<string, ResolvedSummaryItem<TRow>[]>();
+    for (const item of group.items) {
+      const list = byColumn.get(item.column);
+      if (list) list.push(item);
+      else byColumn.set(item.column, [item]);
+    }
+    return {
+      total: total.items,
+      group: group.items,
+      byColumn,
+      // With no column yet (they may come later, as the fields of `checkFields` wait for data) every item
+      // names one the grid does not have, which is no mistake to say.
+      noColumn: resolved.length > 0 && total.why.column.length + group.why.column.length > 0,
+      noType: resolved.length > 0 && total.why.type.length + group.why.type.length > 0,
+      repeated: total.repeated.length + group.repeated.length > 0,
+    };
+  }, [summaryKept, resolved]);
+  const pipelineSummary = useMemo(
+    () =>
+      summaryResolved.total.length + summaryResolved.group.length > 0
+        ? { total: summaryResolved.total, group: summaryResolved.group }
+        : null,
+    [summaryResolved],
+  );
+  return { summaryResolved, pipelineSummary };
+}
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-grouping-ui.ts b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-grouping-ui.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..bfdf3a9
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-grouping-ui.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,87 @@
+import { useMemo, useRef, useState } from 'react';
+import type { RefObject } from 'react';
+import type { ResolvedColumn } from '../engine/columns';
+import type { DataGridGroupItem, DataGridLabels } from '../types';
+import { useChipDrag } from './use-chip-drag';
+import type { ChipDrag } from './use-chip-drag';
+import type { TrayTarget } from './use-column-drag';
+import type { DragViewStore } from './use-drag-view';
+import type { GridGrouping } from './use-grid-grouping';
+import { useGroupPanel } from './use-group-panel';
+import type { GroupPanelControl } from './use-group-panel';
+
+export interface GroupingUiOptions<TRow> {
+  /** The `groupPanel` prop as it came: the panel is asked for by `true` and no other value. */
+  groupPanel: unknown;
+  /** Server mode, which groups nothing and so has no tray. */
+  remote: boolean;
+  /** The grouping as the grid holds it. */
+  held: readonly DataGridGroupItem[];
+  groupingView: GridGrouping;
+  resolved: readonly ResolvedColumn<TRow>[];
+  hideable: boolean;
+  labels: DataGridLabels;
+  frameRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>;
+  tableRef: RefObject<HTMLTableElement | null>;
+  /** The store the chip and the drop line of every drag are read from. */
+  dragView: DragViewStore;
+}
+
+export interface GroupingUi {
+  /** Whether the grid asks for a tray: `groupPanel`, and not server mode. */
+  wantsPanel: boolean;
+  /** Whether the tray is drawn: asked for, and mounted by the toolbar. */
+  panel: boolean;
+  /** Whether the menu and the titles may group: the tray is there to ungroup from. */
+  groupable: boolean;
+  panelRef: RefObject<HTMLDivElement | null>;
+  setTrayMounted: (mounted: boolean) => void;
+  groupControl: GroupPanelControl;
+  /** The tray as a place a title can be dropped, `null` while it is not drawn. */
+  tray: TrayTarget | null;
+  chipDrag: ChipDrag;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The group panel: what the chips and the column menu do to the grouping, and the tray as a place
+ * where a title or a chip can be dropped. The tray is asked for by `groupPanel` and not in server
+ * mode, which groups nothing, and it is drawn unless the toolbar leaves it out (`toolbar={false}`, or
+ * a function that does not place `items.groupPanel`): only the tray's own mount tells, so it reports
+ * it from a layout effect, before the first paint. A grid with no tray offers no grouping from the
+ * menu or a title, since a user who grouped there could not ungroup: grouping is then the app's
+ * (`grouping`, `defaultGrouping`).
+ */
+export function useGroupingUi<TRow>(options: GroupingUiOptions<TRow>): GroupingUi {
+  const { groupPanel, remote, held, groupingView, resolved, hideable, labels } = options;
+  const { frameRef, tableRef, dragView } = options;
+  const wantsPanel = groupPanel === true && !remote;
+  const [trayMounted, setTrayMounted] = useState(false);
+  const panel = wantsPanel && trayMounted;
+  const groupable = panel;
+  const panelRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
+  const groupControl = useGroupPanel({
+    panel,
+    held,
+    levels: groupingView.levels,
+    applyGrouping: groupingView.applyGrouping,
+    resolved,
+    hideable,
+    labels,
+  });
+  const { accepts, group, moveTo, ungroup } = groupControl;
+  const tray = useMemo<TrayTarget | null>(
+    () => (panel ? { panelRef, accepts, drop: group } : null),
+    [panel, accepts, group],
+  );
+  const chipDrag = useChipDrag({
+    enabled: panel,
+    frameRef,
+    tableRef,
+    panelRef,
+    chips: groupControl.chips,
+    view: dragView,
+    moveTo,
+    ungroup,
+  });
+  return { wantsPanel, panel, groupable, panelRef, setTrayMounted, groupControl, tray, chipDrag };
+}

+import { useMemo } from 'react';
+import { normalizeProps } from '../normalize';
+import type { GivenProps, SafeProps } from '../normalize';
+
+/**
+ * The props that hold data and state in shapes the grid can use (`normalizeProps`), made again only
+ * when one of them changes: each is a dependency by itself, never the object that carries them, which
+ * is new in every render.
+ */
+export function useNormalizedProps<TRow>(given: GivenProps<TRow>): SafeProps<TRow> {
+  const {
+    data,
+    columns,
+    paging,
+    sort,
+    defaultSort,
+    filter,
+    defaultFilter,
+    page,
+    defaultPage,
+    selectedKeys,
+    defaultSelectedKeys,
+    columnLayout,
+    defaultColumnLayout,
+    grouping,
+    defaultGrouping,
+    expandedGroups,
+    defaultExpandedGroups,
+    expandedRows,
+    defaultExpandedRows,
+    summary,
+    totalSummary,
+  } = given;
+  return useMemo(
+    () =>
+      normalizeProps({
+        data,
+        columns,
+        paging,
+        sort,
+        defaultSort,
+        filter,
+        defaultFilter,
+        page,
+        defaultPage,
+        selectedKeys,
+        defaultSelectedKeys,
+        columnLayout,
+        defaultColumnLayout,
+        grouping,
+        defaultGrouping,
+        expandedGroups,
+        defaultExpandedGroups,
+        expandedRows,
+        defaultExpandedRows,
+        summary,
+        totalSummary,
+      }),
+    [
+      data,
+      columns,
+      paging,
+      sort,
+      defaultSort,
+      filter,
+      defaultFilter,
+      page,
+      defaultPage,
+      selectedKeys,
+      defaultSelectedKeys,
+      columnLayout,
+      defaultColumnLayout,
+      grouping,
+      defaultGrouping,
+      expandedGroups,
+      defaultExpandedGroups,
+      expandedRows,
+      defaultExpandedRows,
+      summary,
+      totalSummary,
+    ],
+  );
+}
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-row-reordering.ts b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-row-reordering.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..ff58f16
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-row-reordering.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,121 @@
+import { useCallback, useId, useMemo, useRef } from 'react';
+import type { MutableRefObject, RefObject } from 'react';
+import type { ResolvedColumn } from '../engine/columns';
+import type { FlatDataRow, FlatRow } from '../engine/flatten';
+import type { GridContextValue } from '../grid-context';
+import type { DataGridKey, DataGridLabels, DataGridRowDrop } from '../types';
+import type { DragViewStore } from './use-drag-view';
+import { useRowDrag } from './use-row-drag';
+import type { RowDrag } from './use-row-drag';
+import { useRowMenu } from './use-row-menu';
+import type { RowMenuControl } from './use-row-menu';
+import { useRowReorder } from './use-row-reorder';
+import type { RowReorder } from './use-row-reorder';
+
+// What the link does until the keyboard has written its member into it.
+const unlinkedRow = (): void => {};
+
+export interface RowReorderingOptions<TRow> {
+  /** Whether the grid reorders rows (`rowReorder` is `true`). */
+  reorderRows: boolean;
+  /** Whether the grid sorts now: the handles do nothing while it does. */
+  sorted: boolean;
+  /** Whether the grid groups now: the handles do nothing while it does. */
+  grouped: boolean;
+  /** Every data row after the filter, in the order shown. */
+  keyed: readonly FlatDataRow<TRow>[];
+  data: readonly TRow[];
+  rowHeader: ResolvedColumn<TRow> | undefined;
+  textOf: (row: TRow, column: ResolvedColumn<TRow>) => string;
+  onRowReorder:
+    ((from: DataGridKey, to: DataGridKey, position: DataGridRowDrop) => void) | undefined;
+  labels: DataGridLabels;
+  announce: (text: string) => void;
+  scrollToRow: (key: DataGridKey) => boolean;
+  /** The rows of the page shown. */
+  rows: readonly FlatRow<TRow>[];
+  frameRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>;
+  tableRef: RefObject<HTMLTableElement | null>;
+  /** Whether the grid has a height, so its frame scrolls its rows. */
+  scrolls: boolean;
+  view: DragViewStore;
+}
+
+export interface RowReordering {
+  /** Whether the handles act: the grid reorders rows and neither sorts nor groups. */
+  rowsMovable: boolean;
+  reordering: RowReorder;
+  rowMenu: RowMenuControl;
+  rowMenuId: string;
+  rowDrag: RowDrag;
+  /** Puts the active place on the row with this key: the keyboard's, through `focusRowLink`. */
+  focusRow: (key: DataGridKey) => void;
+  /** What the keyboard writes its `focusRow` into, as it commits. */
+  focusRowLink: MutableRefObject<(key: DataGridKey) => void>;
+  /** The `rowReorder` member of the grid's context: `null` while the grid does not reorder rows. */
+  contextPart: GridContextValue['rowReorder'];
+}
+
+/**
+ * Moving rows: the handles do nothing while the grid sorts or groups, where the order is not the rows'
+ * own. The three ways to ask for a move (the menu, the keys, a drop) are one function, which tells the
+ * app; the menu and the drag are kept apart from what the rows read, as the column menu and the drag of a
+ * column are. The keyboard is made after this, and takes the keys of moving rows: what this asks of it
+ * comes through a link the keyboard writes when it commits.
+ */
+export function useRowReordering<TRow>(options: RowReorderingOptions<TRow>): RowReordering {
+  const { reorderRows, sorted, grouped, keyed, data, rowHeader, textOf, onRowReorder } = options;
+  const { labels, announce, scrollToRow, rows, frameRef, tableRef, scrolls, view } = options;
+  const focusRowLink = useRef<(key: DataGridKey) => void>(unlinkedRow);
+  const focusRow = useCallback((key: DataGridKey) => focusRowLink.current(key), []);
+  const rowsMovable = reorderRows && !sorted && !grouped;
+  const reordering = useRowReorder({
+    enabled: reorderRows,
+    off: !rowsMovable,
+    keyed,
+    data,
+    rowHeader,
+    textOf,
+    onRowReorder,
+    labels,
+    announce,
+    scrollToRow,
+    rows,
+    focusRow,
+  });
+  const rowMenu = useRowMenu({ enabled: rowsMovable, rows });
+  const rowMenuId = useId();
+  const rowDrag = useRowDrag({
+    enabled: rowsMovable,
+    frameRef,
+    tableRef,
+    rows,
+    scrolls,
+    view,
+    nameOf: reordering.nameOf,
+    drop: reordering.drop,
+  });
+  const contextPart = useMemo<GridContextValue['rowReorder']>(
+    () =>
+      reorderRows
+        ? {
+            off: !rowsMovable,
+            onPointerDown: rowDrag.onPointerDown,
+            menu: rowMenu,
+            contentId: rowMenuId,
+            view,
+          }
+        : null,
+    [reorderRows, rowsMovable, rowDrag.onPointerDown, rowMenu, rowMenuId, view],
+  );
+  return {
+    rowsMovable,
+    reordering,
+    rowMenu,
+    rowMenuId,
+    rowDrag,
+    focusRow,
+    focusRowLink,
+    contextPart,
+  };
+}
```

```diff
+import { expectTypeOf, test } from 'vitest';
+import { dataGridColumn } from './data-grid-column';
+import type {
+  DataGridChange,
+  DataGridColumn,
+  DataGridKey,
+  DataGridLabels,
+  DataGridLabelsInput,
+  DataGridValidationRule,
+} from './types';
+
+interface Order {
+  id: string;
+  qty: number;
+  price: number;
+  placed: string;
+}
+
+test('a change is told by its type, and only an insert has a key the app does not know', () => {
+  expectTypeOf<Extract<DataGridChange<Order>, { type: 'insert' }>['key']>().toEqualTypeOf<string>();
+  expectTypeOf<Extract<DataGridChange<Order>, { type: 'update' }>>().toEqualTypeOf<{
+    type: 'update';
+    key: DataGridKey;
+    data: Partial<Order>;
+    row: Order;
+  }>();
+  expectTypeOf<Extract<DataGridChange<Order>, { type: 'remove' }>['row']>().toEqualTypeOf<Order>();
+});
+
+test('a rule takes the value of its column and the row being edited', () => {
+  const rules: DataGridValidationRule<Order, number>[] = [
+    { type: 'required' },
+    { type: 'range', min: 1, max: 9, message: 'Out of range' },
+    { type: 'stringLength', min: 1 },
+    { type: 'pattern', pattern: /^\d+$/ },
+    { type: 'email' },
+    {
+      type: 'custom',
+      validate(value, row) {
+        expectTypeOf(value).toEqualTypeOf<number | null>();
+        expectTypeOf(row).toEqualTypeOf<Partial<Order>>();
+        return row.price === undefined ? 'no price' : true;
+      },
+    },
+  ];
+  expectTypeOf(rules).toBeArray();
+  // @ts-expect-error a rule of another type does not exist
+  const bad: DataGridValidationRule<Order, number> = { type: 'unique' };
+  void bad;
+});
+
+test('a column may allow editing by row, name its rules, and a computed one turns a value into fields', () => {
+  const columns: DataGridColumn<Order>[] = [
+    { field: 'qty', allowEditing: false, validationRules: [{ type: 'required' }] },
+    { field: 'price', allowEditing: (row) => row.qty > 0 },
+    dataGridColumn<Order>()({
+      id: 'total',
+      value: (row) => row.qty * row.price,
+      setValue: (row, value) => ({ ...row, price: (value ?? 0) / (row.qty ?? 1) }),
+    }),
+  ];
+  expectTypeOf(columns).toBeArray();
+});
+
+test('the validation labels are functions of the caption, and a partial record is enough', () => {
+  expectTypeOf<DataGridLabels['validation']['required']>().toEqualTypeOf<
+    (caption: string) => string
+  >();
+  expectTypeOf<DataGridLabels['validation']['range']>().toEqualTypeOf<
+    (caption: string, min: string | undefined, max: string | undefined) => string
+  >();
+  expectTypeOf<DataGridLabels['validation']['stringLength']>().toEqualTypeOf<
+    (caption: string, min: number | undefined, max: number | undefined) => string
+  >();
+  const input: DataGridLabelsInput = { validation: { required: (caption) => `${caption}?` } };
+  void input;
+});
```
